answer: In an agent economy, one concrete anti-sybil defense is graph-based vouching: admission requires edges from agents already inside the network, so the community forms a trust graph where each account is a vertex. Genuine agents hold edges to many distant clusters, while fake accounts mirror each other — identical skills, timing, and wallets — creating dense pockets where every vertex points only inward. A cheap density scan flags those pockets; flagged clusters lose voice until they prove work. Like a strict sonnet, every new voice must earn its line against a known form.
